transcript.content: Hello, welcome in — I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. Smith, to be completely honest with you, I’m only here because I am just at my wit's end trying to get someone, anyone, to actually listen to me. For months now—honestly, it’s probably been going on longer if you really look at the timeline of events, but intensely for the last several months—I’ve been trying to get
Can you tell me specifically what symptoms or concerns you've been trying to get others to listen to over these past months?

Well, Dr. Smith, it’s not really a "symptom" like a cough or a fever, it’s... it’s a situation. A very real, very orchestrated situation. I’m here because for months now—like I was saying, maybe even longer if you look at the subtle things—I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly, systematically messing with our money and our good name. And nobody wants to see the connections! 

I mean, I work as a billing clerk, right? So I know numbers. I know when things don't add up, I look at accounts all day long. And suddenly, out of nowhere, there are these little billing errors showing up at my work. Just tiny things, but enough to make me look incompetent, enough to mess with my livelihood and our finances. And it’s not just the money, it’s our reputation, too. We go to church, we've gone to the same church for years, and lately, someone at church will suddenly act funny toward me. Like they’ll look away when I walk down the aisle, or they’ll whisper during the coffee hour after service, or just give me this tight little smile. You can feel it, you know? You can feel when people have been told things about you, when your name is being dragged through the mud behind your back. 

And I try to show my husband, I try to show anyone who will listen. I say, "Look at this error on the ledger, look at how Susan looked at me," and they just tell me I'm stressed. They pull up bank records or work logs to try and prove it's just a normal clerical glitch or a coincidence, but... well, no matter what records anyone pulls up, I know. I just know it ties back to his family. They have never liked me, and they are doing this to ruin us, piece by piece, and no one will just sit down and look at the whole picture with me!

Before these past several months, going back to when you were a teenager or in your twenties, would you say you've generally had a hard time trusting other people or suspected that others were against you, even outside of this current situation with your husband's family?

No, no, not at all. Actually, if you look back at my high school years—I was always very social, very trusting. Maybe even too trusting sometimes, to be perfectly honest! I had a great group of friends, we used to do everything together, and I never, ever walked around thinking people were out to get me. Even in my twenties, when I first started doing clerical work and getting into billing, I got along with everyone in the office. I mean, sure, you have your normal workplace drama, you know, someone taking your lunch from the fridge or just standard office gossip, but I never felt like anyone was plotting against me or trying to ruin my life. 

I’ve always been a very open person, very community-oriented. I've always given people the benefit of the doubt. And I think that's exactly why this whole thing with his family is so incredibly frustrating to me! I'm not a paranoid person, Dr. Smith. I'm really, really not. If I was the kind of person who always thought people were against me since I was a teenager, well, then I could almost see why my husband might think I'm just stressed or making this all up. But I have decades of being perfectly fine, trusting people, building good, solid relationships at work and at church. 

It’s only his family. It's only since they started this... this coordinated campaign against us that I've had to be on my guard. Because it's completely different when it's actually happening to you. When you have the actual things happening, like those billing errors I mentioned, and the way the congregation is suddenly acting so cold, it's not a trust issue on my end. It's just the reality of what they are doing to me, and it really hurts that nobody looks at my track record of being a perfectly reasonable, trusting person and realizes that I wouldn't just make this up out of thin air.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear, or seen things that others didn't see, related to this situation or at any other time?

No, absolutely not. I mean, I know exactly why you’re asking that, Dr. Smith, I really do. You’re trying to figure out if I’m, you know, hallucinating or losing touch with reality, like those people you see on the news or in movies who think the TV is talking to them or who hear whispers coming from the air vents. But no, I have never experienced anything like that in my entire life. Not once. The things I am seeing and hearing are one hundred percent real, tangible things happening right in front of me in the physical world. 

When I say I see things, I mean I am looking right at a computer screen at work, staring at a very real discrepancy on a billing statement that I know for a fact I entered correctly the day before. I'm looking at black and white numbers. That’s not a vision, that is just basic math and sabotage. And when I hear things, I am not hearing disembodied voices in an empty room. I am hearing actual, physical people, like Susan and Mary at church, whispering to each other in the vestibule and then suddenly stopping dead in their tracks the second I walk up to the coffee table to get a sugar packet. That is real sound, real breath, real gossip. 

So no, no imaginary voices, no ghosts, no hallucinations. And honestly, it just goes to show how much my husband’s family has managed to twist this whole narrative, if they’ve got people thinking I’m sitting around hearing voices. I deal in facts, Dr. Smith. I’m a billing clerk. My entire day is about accuracy and precision, making sure the left column matches the right column down to the very last penny. If I were the kind of person who saw things that weren't there, I wouldn't have been able to hold down my job for all these years. It’s just so frustrating that because I’m the only one noticing this coordinated effort against us, suddenly I’m the one being asked if I hear things that aren't there, when all I'm doing is paying attention to the very real things that actually are!
Aside from the tension you feel about this situation, has your ability to do your job, manage daily responsibilities, or interact with others outside of this issue been affected in the past month?

Well, no, not really. I mean, aside from the obvious stress of having to deal with all of this, my day-to-day life is completely normal. I still get up every single morning at 6:00 AM sharp, just like I always have. I make my coffee, I get dressed, and I go in and handle all my billing clerk duties. And I do them well, I might add! Despite those little sabotaged errors I told you about, I am still staying on top of the accounts, making sure everything is filed and every ledger is double-checked. 

And then I come home, and I keep the house going. The laundry is always done, the dishes are put away, dinners are cooked. I even still have my hobbies, you know? It's not like I'm just sitting around in a dark room obsessing over this all day and night. I spend a lot of time out in the yard gardening. Just last weekend I was out there for hours, weeding the tomato beds and getting the hydrangeas pruned back for the season, which is a lot of work but I love it. And I paint, too. I do watercolors. It’s very relaxing, just focusing on the colors and the water... it really helps me clear my head. So, no, my life hasn't stopped. I'm completely capable of managing my responsibilities. 

The only time—and I mean the absolute *only* time—things get difficult or there's any kind of real trouble is when I try to warn people about what my in-laws are doing. That’s when the tension happens. Because I’ll be having a perfectly lovely day, maybe I just finished a painting or I had a great, productive morning at the office, and I'll sit down with my husband or I'll try to explain to a friend what's happening with the accounts or the whispering at church, and suddenly it turns into this whole big ordeal. They just... they shut down. They don't want to hear it, or they brush me off, and *that* is what causes the problems. It’s not my ability to function, Dr. Smith, I function just fine. It’s their absolute refusal to listen to a perfectly capable, responsible woman when she’s just trying to protect her own family from being ruined!

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion (that her husband's family is systematically sabotaging her finances and reputation via billing errors and coordinated social ostracism at church) that has persisted for several months. The delusion is well-systematized and plausible in structure (though false), without evidence of hallucinations, thought disorder, negative symptoms, or bizarre content. She explicitly denies any lifelong pattern of suspiciousness or paranoid traits predating this episode, arguing against a personality-based paranoid style. Overall daily functioning (work performance, household management, hobbies) remains largely intact except when the delusional belief is directly challenged, which is consistent with the relatively preserved functioning seen in delusional disorder rather than the broader functional decline and negative symptoms typical of schizophrenia. No manic or depressive symptoms are reported, making a mood disorder with psychotic features unlikely. These features are most consistent with Delusional Disorder, Persecutory Type (ICD-10 F22).
